request_text: I need help taking Claridi.ai to market. I built a strategic intelligence methodology, automated it into a reasoning engine, and realized the opportunity is much bigger than the original brand strategy use case. Claridi can help people make better decisions before they execute, and potentially serve as a strategy layer inside AI tools and business platforms. I’ve gotten it surprisingly far on my own, but I need guidance on protecting the IP, validating the business model, raising capital, building the right team, partnerships/licensing, and scaling it into a real company.

## Company
Claridi.ai's own site could not be read: claridi.ai and www.claridi.ai are blocked by this environment's network policy [unsupported]. No search result about Claridi.ai itself was found; what the company does comes only from the requester's own words on the intake form: a strategic intelligence methodology automated into a reasoning engine that helps people make better decisions before they execute, with a possible role as a strategy layer inside AI tools and business platforms (LinkedIn project request, 2026-09-24) [needs stipulation].

## Evidence of stage
From the request: the founder built the methodology and the engine largely alone, and is now asking for help with IP protection, business-model validation, raising capital, team, partnerships and licensing, and scaling (LinkedIn project request) [needs stipulation]. Founding date, headcount, funding and customers: not found.

## Market and buyer
US business AI use held between 17% and 20% of firms from December 2025 to May 2026, with 20% to 23% expecting to use AI within six months ([Census Bureau, May 2026](https://www.census.gov/library/stories/2026/05/ai-use-businesses.html)) [supported]. As of 3 May 2026 the Information sector (39.7%) and Finance and Insurance (33.9%) were well above the national rate of 19.8% ([Census BTOS, 7 May 2026](https://www.census.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2026/btos-may-7.html)) [supported]. Fewer than 20% of firms with four or fewer employees used AI ([Census Bureau, May 2026](https://www.census.gov/library/stories/2026/05/ai-use-businesses.html)) [supported].

## Competitors
Decision-intelligence platforms named in 2026 industry roundups include Aera Technology, FICO, SAS, IBM, Quantexa, Palantir Foundry, Diwo, Taktile and Board International ([Eyko, 2026](https://eyko.ai/blog/decision-intelligence-landscape-2026/)) [needs stipulation]. Where Claridi.ai positions against them is not found.

## Adjacent
The requester's LinkedIn profile (the one on the intake form) describes a brand strategist working on positioning and messaging ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/kristingludwick/)) [needs stipulation]; a profile listing names her as brand and marketing strategist at Ludwick Consulting ([Intch](https://intch.org/16425539)) [needs stipulation]. This matches the request's "original brand strategy use case". Partners, investors and customers of Claridi.ai: not found.

## Macroeconomic context
The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by a quarter point to 3-3/4 to 4 percent on 16 September 2026, citing elevated inflation alongside robust capital investment ([Federal Reserve, 16 Sep 2026](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/files/monetary20260916a1.pdf)) [supported]. Business investment in Q2 2026 rose on equipment and intellectual property products, including software and R&D ([BEA, 26 Aug 2026](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/gdp-second-estimate-and-corporate-profits-2nd-quarter-2026)) [supported]. The SBIR/STTR programs were reauthorized through 30 September 2031 ([SBA, 13 Apr 2026](https://www.sba.gov/article/2026/04/13/administrator-loeffler-applauds-sbir-sttr-reauthorization)) [supported], and NSF's America's Seed Fund lists artificial intelligence among the areas it funds ([NSF Seed Fund](https://seedfund.nsf.gov/)) [supported]. The USPTO's November 2025 revised guidance applies the ordinary inventorship standard to AI-assisted inventions and does not allow AI as an inventor ([USPTO, 2025](https://www.uspto.gov/subscription-center/2025/revised-inventorship-guidance-ai-assisted-inventions)) [supported]. The Copyright Office found that AI outputs are protected only where a human author determined sufficient expressive elements, and that prompts alone are not enough ([Copyright Office, 29 Jan 2025](https://copyright.gov/ai/Copyright-and-Artificial-Intelligence-Part-2-Copyrightability-Report.pdf)) [supported]. Cycle position: rates rising again, investment in software and R&D still growing, and federal seed funding secured through 2031.

## Signals worth a conversation
1. The request names six workstreams at once — IP, business model, capital, team, partnerships and licensing, scale — which cannot all be first (LinkedIn project request) [needs stipulation].
2. IP rules for AI-assisted work turn on documented human contribution ([USPTO, 2025](https://www.uspto.gov/subscription-center/2025/revised-inventorship-guidance-ai-assisted-inventions)) [supported].
3. Rates rose on 16 September 2026, which raises the bar for early-stage capital ([Federal Reserve, 16 Sep 2026](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/files/monetary20260916a1.pdf)) [supported].
4. Non-dilutive federal seed funding for AI is authorized through 2031 ([SBA, 13 Apr 2026](https://www.sba.gov/article/2026/04/13/administrator-loeffler-applauds-sbir-sttr-reauthorization)) [supported].
